title: Parul Chaudhary Clocks India's Second-Fastest Steeplechase at Shanghai Diamond League
excerpt: The national record holder finished seventh in a world-class field with 9:12.84, missing her own Indian record by just 0.38 seconds in her first race of 2026.
body:
Parul Chaudhary announced her 2026 season in emphatic fashion at the Shanghai Diamond League on Friday, clocking 9 minutes 12.84 seconds in the women's 3,000-metre steeplechase — the second-fastest time ever recorded by an Indian athlete — to finish seventh in a brutally competitive field.

A near-miss on her own record

The time fell just 0.38 seconds short of Chaudhary's national record of 9:12.46, set at the 2025 Diamond League in Doha. For context, that gap is roughly the length of a single stride in a steeplechase. Her Shanghai run confirmed that the 30-year-old from Uttar Pradesh has returned from the off-season in peak condition, with her water-jump technique and late-race stamina both sharper than in recent outings.

World-class company

The race was won by Uganda's Chemutai Peruth in a blistering 8:51.47, with Kenya's Faith Cherotich taking second in a photo finish. Chaudhary, competing against athletes who collectively hold Olympic and World Championship medals, stayed in contact with the lead pack through 2,000 metres before the East African runners pulled clear. Her seventh-place finish in such a field is a performance that would have won medals at several recent Asian Games.

Building toward bigger targets

This was Chaudhary's first competitive outing since the 2025 World Championships, making it effectively a season opener. Distance runners typically peak later in the year, and a sub-9:13 performance in May suggests she is well ahead of schedule. The 2026 calendar includes the Asian Games qualifiers, the Diamond League circuit, and the possibility of a late-season tilt at the national record.

From Meerut to the world stage

Chaudhary's trajectory — from a small-town athlete in Meerut to India's foremost steeplechaser — mirrors the slow but steady rise of Indian distance running on the global stage. She won Asian Games silver in 2023, became the first Indian woman to break 9:15 in the steeplechase, and has now posted two sub-9:13 performances in elite international fields. In a country where cricket dominates sports coverage, her Diamond League results are a reminder that Indian athletes are making inroads in events where they were once invisible.

For the diaspora watching from afar

Indian athletics rarely makes the highlight reels that NRI sports fans see on their feeds. But Chaudhary's growing consistency at the Diamond League level — the highest tier of track and field below the Olympics — is exactly the kind of story that signals a deeper shift in Indian sport. Watch for her name as the season unfolds.
